description: Structured capability cards for the harnesses and model families a TypeSafe (Jev) routing pass can choose between. Synthetic and public-knowledge only. Authored by a coding agent, not generated by Jev.

band_vocabulary.cheap: Fast, low-cost model for lookups, rewrites, and single-step asks.
band_vocabulary.mid: Balanced model for multi-step work, light research, and file edits.
band_vocabulary.frontier: Highest-capability model for ambiguous, high-stakes, or long-horizon work.
band_vocabulary.unassigned: No band: this family's name matches no pricing heuristic we can defend.

harnesses.what: OpenAI's Codex CLI in a sandboxed shell. It reads and patches files, runs builds and tests, and iterates against real command output. Strongest when the task is a precise change to code that already exists and there is a pass/fail signal to iterate against.
not_for: Work that depends on MCP servers, skills, or delegated subagents — it has none.
Open-ended web research; there is no first-class browsing loop.
Driving a browser or judging a rendered UI.
harnesses.context: Terminal only, network-restricted sandbox by default, with approvals gating escalation. Five OpenAI models, all frontier-or-near.
examples: Fix the failing assertion in `parser.test.ts` and keep the rest of the suite green.
Apply this 40-line diff across six call sites and run the type checker.
Bisect which of the last ten commits broke the build.
Port this module from CommonJS to ESM and prove it with the existing tests.

harnesses.what: Anthropic's Claude Code CLI, with the widest tool surface of any harness here: MCP servers, skills, hooks, background tasks, delegated subagents, web fetch and search, and a plan mode for designing before editing. Choose it when the work is ambiguous, spans many files, or needs a tool no other harness carries.
not_for: A one-line lookup, where its startup and context cost dominates the work.
Reaching a non-Anthropic model — it carries Anthropic models only.
harnesses.context: Terminal, IDE extension, desktop, and web. Six Anthropic models spanning Haiku through Opus, so the cheap-to-frontier decision is available inside the harness.
examples: Read the Linear ticket over MCP, then implement it across the repo.
Design the migration before touching anything; show me the plan first.
Audit every call site of this API and tell me which ones are unsafe.
Run the repo's review skill over this branch and summarize what it found.

harnesses.what: An aggregator harness fronting a few hundred models across the Codex and OpenRouter namespaces behind one agent loop. The reason to pick it is the model, not the tooling: comparing vendors, or reaching a specific third-party model by name.
not_for: Work whose difficulty is tooling rather than model choice.
Anything that leans on harness-specific features such as skills or hooks.
harnesses.context: 402 models on this machine under the `openai-codex/` and `openrouter/` prefixes. Descriptions are sparse, so the model names are most of what routing gets.
examples: Run this same prompt against a Gemini model and an OpenAI model and diff the answers.
Use DeepSeek for this — I want to see how it handles the algorithm.
Which open-weight model can summarize this transcript acceptably for a tenth the cost?

harnesses.what: Cursor driven over ACP. Editor-native: it sees the open workspace through Cursor's own index and semantic codebase search, and its Composer models are tuned for fast, well-scoped edits inside a project that is already open.
not_for: Headless or CI runs where no editor is attached.
Long autonomous sessions; it is built around short interactive turns.
Reaching models outside Cursor's own roster.
harnesses.context: Requires an attached, signed-in Cursor workspace. On the machine this dataset was captured from it reported no models at all, which is itself the routing signal: do not propose a harness that cannot run.
examples: Rename this symbol everywhere in the open project and fix the imports.
Where in this codebase do we already do something like this?
Tighten up the component I have open — same behavior, less code.

harnesses.what: omp over ACP, the broadest model aggregator available: hundreds of models across the Cursor, Codex, OpenRouter, and xAI namespaces under one agent loop. The reason to choose it is reach — a model that no other harness carries.
not_for: Work that needs a specific harness feature; omp routes models, it is not a tool platform.
Cases where you cannot name the model you want — the catalog is far too large to browse.
harnesses.context: 666 models on this machine, collapsing to 442 families — and every single description is empty. That emptiness is the gap these cards exist to fill.
examples: Use Qwen for this one; I want a non-US-vendor model on it.
I need `cursor/composer-2.5` specifically — route me there.
Try the cheapest model that can still get this refactor right, whoever makes it.

harnesses.what: xAI's Grok Build over ACP, carrying exactly one model. Fast turns and current-events grounding from xAI's own stack. Because the roster is a single model, picking this harness settles the model question too.
not_for: Large multi-file refactors.
Work that needs a specific non-xAI model.
harnesses.context: One model, `grok-4.5`, which is also the default. The second routing question has nothing to decide.
examples: What changed in this API in the last week?
Quick script to pull down and chart this feed.
Give me the current state of play on this, then stub the client.

harnesses.what: Hermes Agent over ACP: a persistent agent that carries state across sessions instead of starting fresh each thread. Choose it for a standing responsibility — something monitored, revisited, or handed forward — rather than for a single edit.
not_for: A quick one-off change; the persistence is overhead with no payoff.
Throwaway experiments you would rather it did not remember.
harnesses.context: 41 curated models with vendor-prefixed ids, defaulting to a long-context Codex model. The only harness here where a thread is expected to outlive the conversation that started it.
examples: Own the dependency upgrades for this repo and keep at it week over week.
Watch this dashboard and tell me when the error rate moves.
Keep working the migration backlog; pick up where you left off last time.

families.label: GPT-6-Astra
families.what: OpenAI's current flagship. The strongest general reasoner in this catalog for long-horizon agentic coding: holds a large plan across many tool calls without drifting.
not_for: Lookups, renames, and single-file edits — the capability is wasted and the bill is not.
High-volume batch work where per-call cost compounds.
families.context: Default model on Codex and on omp; also reachable through Hermes.
examples: Redesign this module's boundaries and carry the refactor through the whole repo.
Work this ambiguous bug report down to a root cause and a fix.

families.label: GPT-5.6-Sol
families.what: The reasoning-leaning member of the GPT-5.6 trio. Slower and more deliberate than its siblings; a reasonable step down from the flagship when the work is hard but bounded.
not_for: Latency-sensitive interactive turns.
Trivial edits that do not need deliberation.
families.context: Codex only in the captured shortlist. Its name matches no pricing heuristic, so its band is unassigned rather than guessed.
examples: Work out why this race condition only reproduces under load.
Design the schema migration and justify the ordering.

families.label: GPT-5.6-Terra
families.what: The throughput-leaning member of the GPT-5.6 trio. Built for steady mechanical work across many files rather than for a single hard judgement.
not_for: Ambiguous design questions with no clear success criterion.
families.context: Codex only in the captured shortlist. Band unassigned — the name carries no pricing signal we can read.
examples: Apply this lint rule fix across all 200 violations.
Convert every test in this directory to the new helper.

families.label: GPT-5.6-Luna
families.what: The latency-leaning member of the GPT-5.6 trio. Fast interactive turns at the cost of depth; the one to reach for when the loop is conversational.
not_for: Long autonomous runs.
Problems whose answer depends on sustained reasoning.
families.context: Codex only in the captured shortlist. Band unassigned.
examples: Walk me through what this function does, then tweak the edge case.
Quick pass on this PR description.

families.label: GPT-5.5
families.what: The previous-generation general model. Still competent across ordinary implementation work and widely available, which makes it a safe fallback when a newer family is not offered.
not_for: Work at the edge of current capability.
Very long contexts.
families.context: Default model on Pi; also in Codex's shortlist. Band unassigned.
examples: Implement this endpoint against the spec in the issue.
Add retry and backoff to this client.

families.label: GPT-5.6-Sol (900k context)
families.what: GPT-5.6-Sol with a 900k-token window. The distinguishing feature is the context, not the reasoning: it is the family to pick when the whole corpus must be in the prompt at once.
not_for: Short prompts, where the long-context premium buys nothing.
families.context: Hermes Agent's default. The `-900k` suffix survives family collapse, so this is a distinct family from `gpt-5.6-sol`. Band unassigned.
examples: Read all 40 of these transcripts and find the contradictions.
Hold the entire service in context and trace this request end to end.

families.label: Claude Fable 5.1
families.what: Anthropic's writing- and judgement-leaning frontier family. Best in this catalog for prose, review, and calls that hinge on taste rather than on passing a test.
not_for: Lookups, renames, and single-file edits — the capability is wasted and the bill is not.
High-volume batch work where per-call cost compounds.
Tight mechanical loops where a cheaper model measurably matches it.
families.context: Offered by Claude Code; also present in the Pi and omp catalogs.
examples: Review this design doc and tell me where the argument breaks.
Rewrite this README so a new contributor can follow it.

families.label: Claude Opus 5
families.what: Anthropic's current flagship. The strongest option here for ambiguous, high-stakes, long-horizon agentic work — the cases where being wrong is expensive and the path is not laid out.
not_for: Lookups, renames, and single-file edits — the capability is wasted and the bill is not.
High-volume batch work where per-call cost compounds.
families.context: Claude Code's default, offered there with a 1M window; also reachable through Hermes and omp.
examples: Figure out the right architecture for this before we commit to it.
Own this incident: find the cause, fix it, and prove the fix.

families.label: Claude Opus 4.8
families.what: The prior Opus generation. Close to current-flagship quality on most coding work and worth naming when a thread needs continuity with earlier runs on the same family.
not_for: Lookups, renames, and single-file edits — the capability is wasted and the bill is not.
High-volume batch work where per-call cost compounds.
families.context: Offered by Claude Code with a 1M window and by Hermes Agent.
examples: Continue the refactor we started on 4.8 so the style stays consistent.
Hard multi-file change with no test coverage to lean on.

families.label: Claude Opus 4.7
families.what: An older Opus generation, kept available for reproducibility. Pick it deliberately, to match a previous run, rather than on capability grounds.
not_for: Lookups, renames, and single-file edits — the capability is wasted and the bill is not.
High-volume batch work where per-call cost compounds.
New work, where a newer Opus is strictly better.
families.context: Offered by Claude Code and Hermes Agent.
examples: Reproduce the result we got on 4.7 last quarter.
Re-run this eval on the older Opus for comparison.

families.label: Claude Opus 4.6
families.what: An older Opus generation retained by Hermes. Reproducibility only.
not_for: Lookups, renames, and single-file edits — the capability is wasted and the bill is not.
High-volume batch work where per-call cost compounds.
New work.
families.context: Hermes Agent only in the captured shortlist.
examples: Re-run the 4.6 baseline for the comparison table.
Match the behavior of the agent we shipped on 4.6.

families.label: Claude Opus 4.5
families.what: An older Opus generation retained by Hermes. Reproducibility only.
not_for: Lookups, renames, and single-file edits — the capability is wasted and the bill is not.
High-volume batch work where per-call cost compounds.
New work.
families.context: Hermes Agent only. Its date suffix collapses away, so `claude-opus-4-5-20251101` and any later dated build are one family.
examples: Reproduce the 4.5 run exactly.
Check whether this regression predates 4.6.

families.label: Claude Opus 4
families.what: The original Opus 4. Well below current families on agentic coding; present for historical comparison and for third-party catalogs that have not refreshed.
not_for: Lookups, renames, and single-file edits — the capability is wasted and the bill is not.
High-volume batch work where per-call cost compounds.
Any new work where a later Opus is offered.
families.context: Reaches the shortlist on Pi and Hermes because those catalogs are wide and older entries rank on the `opus` name alone.
examples: Establish the historical baseline for this benchmark.
Confirm the behavior difference between Opus 4 and Opus 5 here.

families.label: Claude Sonnet 5
families.what: Anthropic's balanced family: the default choice for ordinary implementation work that is more than a one-liner but does not need a frontier model. Good tool use, fast enough to stay interactive.
not_for: Genuinely ambiguous architecture calls.
Work where a wrong answer is expensive to discover later.
families.context: Offered by Claude Code; also reachable through Hermes and omp.
examples: Add the feature described in this ticket and its tests.
Wire this new config option through the three places that read it.

families.label: Claude Haiku 4.5
families.what: Anthropic's fast, cheap family. Genuinely capable on bounded single-step work — extraction, classification, mechanical rewrites — at a fraction of the cost of the tiers above it.
not_for: Multi-step agentic work.
Anything requiring sustained reasoning or design judgement.
families.context: Claude Code's cheap option and the only sub-mid Anthropic family in that harness's shortlist. Pi carries a dotted `claude-haiku-4.5`, which collapses to a different family key — see the README.
examples: Pull the version numbers out of this changelog into a table.
Fix the typo in the error string.

families.label: Claude Opus 4.6 (Cursor build)
families.what: Cursor's own packaging of Opus 4.6, exposed with effort suffixes (`-high`, `-max`) that collapse into one family. Frontier reasoning delivered through Cursor's editor context rather than a bare shell.
not_for: Lookups, renames, and single-file edits — the capability is wasted and the bill is not.
High-volume batch work where per-call cost compounds.
Headless runs with no editor attached.
families.context: Reachable only through omp's `cursor/` namespace in the captured snapshot: the Cursor harness itself reported no models. It does NOT survive omp's 8-slot shortlist — see the README.
examples: Hard architectural change, with the whole indexed project in play.
Untangle this dependency cycle across the open workspace.

families.label: Gemini 3 Flash
families.what: Google's fast, cheap tier. High throughput and a large context for the price; adequate on bounded tasks, thin on sustained agentic reasoning.
not_for: Multi-step agentic coding.
Work where subtle correctness matters more than speed.
families.context: Reachable through omp's `cursor/` namespace.
examples: Summarize these 50 log files into one report.
Classify each of these issues by component.

families.label: Gemini 3.5 Flash
families.what: A point revision of the Gemini Flash line. Same cheap-and-fast profile as its siblings; the version number is the only thing distinguishing it at routing time.
not_for: Multi-step agentic coding.
Anything where the version difference from a neighbouring Flash actually matters — it rarely does.
families.context: In both Pi's and omp's shortlists. Five near-identical Flash families crowd those shortlists — see the README.
examples: Turn this transcript into bullet points.
Extract every TODO comment in the repo into a list.

families.label: Gemini 3.6 Flash
families.what: A point revision of the Gemini Flash line. Cheap, fast, long-context; indistinguishable from its neighbours for routing purposes.
not_for: Multi-step agentic coding.
Work needing sustained reasoning.
families.context: In both Pi's and omp's shortlists.
examples: Batch-rewrite these product blurbs.
Diff these two config dumps and tell me what changed.

families.label: Gemini 3.7 Flash
families.what: A point revision of the Gemini Flash line. Cheap, fast, long-context; the routing-relevant profile is identical to the other Flash families.
not_for: Multi-step agentic coding.
Work needing sustained reasoning.
families.context: In both Pi's and omp's shortlists.
examples: Tag each of these support tickets with a severity.
Condense this 200-page spec into a one-page brief.

families.label: Gemini 3.8 Flash
families.what: The newest Gemini Flash point revision here. Cheap and fast; the one to prefer among the Flash families purely because it is latest.
not_for: Multi-step agentic coding.
Work needing sustained reasoning.
families.context: In both Pi's and omp's shortlists.
examples: Normalize these 5,000 addresses.
Summarize what each file in this directory is for.

families.label: Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite
families.what: The cheapest tier Google offers here — below Flash. For very high volume, very low difficulty work where per-call cost is the whole constraint.
not_for: Anything involving code edits.
Multi-step work of any kind.
Judgement calls.
families.context: In both Pi's and omp's shortlists.
examples: Is each of these lines a question or a statement?
Strip the boilerplate header off each of these files.

families.label: Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite
families.what: A point revision of the Flash Lite line. Cheapest tier; same profile as its 3.1 sibling.
not_for: Anything involving code edits.
Multi-step work of any kind.
Judgement calls.
families.context: In both Pi's and omp's shortlists. Two Flash Lite families plus five Flash families take seven of omp's eight slots.
examples: Label each row with its language.
Drop the duplicate entries out of this list.

families.label: Grok 4.5
families.what: xAI's current model. Fast, competent on ordinary implementation, and grounded in more recent real-world information than most families here.
not_for: Large multi-file refactors.
Work where the answer must be reproducible against an older run.
families.context: Grok Build's only model, and its default; also reachable through omp.
examples: Build a client for this API as it exists today.
What is the current recommended way to do this, and implement it.

families.label: Grok 4.6 (Cursor build)
families.what: Cursor's packaging of a newer Grok, exposed with `-fast` variants that collapse into one family. Fast turns with Cursor's editor context.
not_for: Headless runs.
Long autonomous sessions.
families.context: Reachable only through omp's `cursor/` namespace in the captured snapshot. Does NOT survive omp's 8-slot shortlist.
examples: Quick edit across the files I have open.
Explain this function and then simplify it.

families.label: Cursor Composer 2.5
families.what: Cursor's in-house model, tuned specifically for fast, well-scoped edits inside an indexed project. On that narrow task it is the best value here; off it, it is unremarkable.
not_for: Design and architecture questions.
Work outside an indexed Cursor workspace.
General reasoning or prose.
families.context: Reachable only through omp's `cursor/` namespace in the captured snapshot. Does NOT survive omp's 8-slot shortlist, despite `composer` carrying an explicit PREFERENCE_RULES weight.
examples: Apply this pattern to the other four components.
Rename this prop everywhere it is used.
